correctness.rationale: For K=-K, Minkowski averaging a translated rectangle with its reflection centralizes it without perimeter loss. Equal-length half-diagonals p,q yield perimeter 2(||p+q||+||p-q||). Separate convexity maximizes this over all of K×K at a pair of vertices; cyclicity makes every nonparallel vertex pair equal norm and therefore a feasible rectangle, attaining the unrestricted maximum. For independent p,q the Hessian of F(.,q) is positive definite because p+q and p−q are independent, excluding any nonvertex maximizers; a radius-R parallelogram identity eliminates any off-center maximizer. Circumcircle chord identities give 4sqrt(2)R cos(defect/2); the sorted projective-angle grid admits an O(m) closest-perpendicular scan. Regular parity counts, hexagon normalization, and n^-2 deficit follow exactly. The actual bundled verify_rectangle.py ran successfully: VERIFY_OK regular_cases=300 cyclic_polygons=104 interior_rectangle_checks=26000. Finite diagnostics do not certify the universal statement.

value.rationale: Maximum-perimeter rectangles are a well-motivated geometric optimization objective (as confirmed by Cabello et al. 2014 and earlier area/perimeter discussion). On the natural centrally symmetric cyclic family, the theorem converts unrestricted continuous rectangle placement into a finite nearest-perpendicular diameter problem, proves rigidity of every extremizer, and yields an O(m) exact geometric scan versus prior O(m³) general algorithms. It includes sharp mod-four exact regular-polygon values and a nontrivial n^-2 deficit from the disk bound. Its structural formula, full equality classification, and computational consequence constitute value beyond routine substitution or finite numerical experimentation.
